podcast.title: Jamaican Sound System Popularity
podcast.body: Like much New Orleans R&B, Shirley and Lee's music was hugely popular among Jamaican sound system audiences. This popularity influenced Coxsone Dodd's decision to seek out a singer with a similar voice to Shirley Goodman, leading to his discovery of Millie Small. "Like much new Orleans R&B, Shirley and Lee were hugely popular among the sound system listeners."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Minor US Chart Success & Imitators
podcast.body: Despite their popularity among sound system listeners in Jamaica, Shirley and Lee only achieved minor chart success in the United States. However, their distinctive sound spawned numerous imitators, including Jean and Eunice and Mickey and Sylvia. "Shirley and Lee only had minor charts success in the US, but spawned a host of emitators, including Jean and Eunice and Mickey and Sylvia."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: New Orleans R&B Duo (1950s)
podcast.body: Shirley and Lee were a New Orleans R&B duo who achieved a string of hits in the early and mid-1950s. Their sound was characterized by pairing Leonard Lee's baritone voice with Shirley Goodman's soprano. "they were a new Orleans R&B duo who had a string of hits in the early and mid-50s, recorded at Kassimon Metassa's studio, pairing Leonard Lee's baritone voice with Shirley Goodman's Saffano."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Recording Studio (1950s)
podcast.body: The duo recorded their hits in the early and mid-1950s at Cosimo Matassa's studio, a prominent recording facility for New Orleans R&B. "recorded at Kassimon Metassa's studio."
